clue.text: Trap in speech for prime minister

indicators.note: in speech means the word for trap is said out loud, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: a pit is a trap dug for animals

explanation.surface: A politician is caught out by a careless remark in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder and the Younger were both British prime ministers; the surname is pronounced like the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Pitts, father and son, led British governments in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Valuable to secure commander showing early talent

indicators.note: to secure means the valuable word holds the commander abbreviation within it

parts.note: precious means of great value
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A valuable asset is used to lock in a commander who shows promise early.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child has developed abilities far earlier than usual for their age.

clue.text: Hear sound of clock that may be over head

indicators.note: Hear means the clock sound is said out loud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: tick-tock is the sound a clock makes

explanation.surface: Listen to the clock that may be ticking overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a clock on the wall above; it means a hat worn on the head, as a chef's tall white hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a hat, such as a chef's tall white one, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Armed cover for officer attending board meeting

definitions.text: Armed cover for officer attending board meeting

parts.words: Armed cover for officer attending board meeting
parts.note: a garment with sleeves (arms) worn by an officer sitting down to dine (board, as in bed and board) with fellow officers, not at a company board meeting

explanation.surface: An officer needs suitable protective wear to sit in on a directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is the old word for a dining table and meals, and 'armed' means having sleeves, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: This short formal jacket is worn by military officers at dinners in their dining hall.

clue.text: Fry in the blaze I ignited

indicators.note: something ignited is set alight and transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something fries in the flames once a fire has been lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' looks like cooking; it is Elizabeth Fry, the English prison reformer pictured on the old five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Fry, Quaker prison reformer, so the surname leads to her first name.

clue.text: Not entirely regular role

indicators.note: Not entirely means the word for regular loses its final letter

parts.note: steady means regular, as in a steady pace

explanation.surface: A job that is not entirely regular work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead means place or role, as in standing in someone's stead.

clue.text: One evaluating a second speaker?

parts.note: a sayer is one who says something, a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone assessing a second person giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An assayer tests metals and ores to judge their purity and worth.

clue.text: Croaking in agony, punctured by first of bites from this?

definitions.text: Croaking in agony, punctured by first of bites from this?

indicators.note: punctured by means a letter is pushed into the rearranged letters
in agony means the letters of croaking are writhing and rearranged
first of means only the opening letter of bites is used

explanation.surface: Someone dies in pain after being bitten, and the clue asks which snake did it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CROAKING and push in B, the first letter of 'bites'. The whole clue also works as the definition: dying from a bite by this snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's longest venomous snake, whose bite can kill a person.

clue.text: Centre of population fashionable society gives wide berth?

indicators.note: gives, with berth, means the society word makes room for the cricket letter inside it
berth completes gives berth: the outer word gives a place to the letter

parts.note: the ton is fashionable high society
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide ball

explanation.surface: In the heart of town, smart society avoids someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives wide berth' looks like avoiding something; here TON literally gives room to W.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a settled place where people live together, a centre of population.

clue.text: Seal has little water-bird by the ears

indicators.note: by the ears means judged by listening, so the bird word is said out loud

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: A seal holds a young bird by the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' here means a stamp, not the sea animal, and 'by the ears' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small seal, often set in a ring, used to stamp documents.

clue.text: Lovely wife no longer is entirely kept

parts.note: a former wife is an ex

indicators.note: kept means the word is is held inside the word for entirely

parts.note: quite can mean entirely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: A man notes that his former wife is still being supported, and very well too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exquisite is extremely beautiful or delicate, a strong synonym for lovely.

clue.text: Force is evil to use against partners

indicators.note: the pair is set against, next to, the word for evil

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing or evil
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that it is wicked to turn on their own partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South and East-West play as partnerships, so 'partners' can be E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular strength or power, so it can stand for force.

clue.text: Pacific group Orwell depicted at war

definitions.meaning: the islands of the central and south Pacific taken together
in Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four this superstate is permanently at war with Eurasia or Eastasia

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both the Pacific island region and Orwell's fictional superstate.

clue.text: Gamble stopping railway in a cloud of steam

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging, the railway filling a gap inside the gamble word
in confirms the railway abbreviation is placed within the word for gamble

parts.note: to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: A gamble halts a steam railway, wreathed in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cloud' is a stage effect: solid carbon dioxide gives off a thick white vapour that looks like steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen carbon dioxide gives off billowing white vapour used for theatrical steam and fog effects.

clue.text: Throw people out of country over time for behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the next piece comes below the earlier ones

parts.note: to deport is to throw people out of a country, and people gives men
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: People are thrown out of the country after a time for bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is the way a person carries and conducts themselves, their bearing and behaviour.

clue.text: Russian leader's dismissive review of Denisovich film?

definitions.text: Russian leader's dismissive review of Denisovich film?

parts.words: Russian leader's dismissive review of Denisovich film?
parts.note: a tsar's name read as a curt verdict on a film of Solzhenitsyn's One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich, calling it bad

explanation.surface: A Russian leader dismisses a film of Solzhenitsyn's novel in a scathing review.
explanation.walkthrough: The tsar's title splits as 'Ivan: the terrible', the kind of one-line review a critic might give.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, the first Russian tsar, earned this epithet for his cruelty.

clue.text: Lion-tamer leans out to fasten rope up

indicators.note: to fasten means the rope word is clasped inside the rearranged letters
out means the letters of leans are put out of order and rearranged
in a down clue, up means the rope word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A lion-tamer leans out of a cage to tie a rope up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters into ANLES; 'up' turns the rope word to read DROC. 'Lion-tamer' is generous: Androcles befriended the lion rather than training it.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend, Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw and was later spared by it.

clue.text: Hold secret hearing — throws for execution on gallows trapdoor.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece is placed on top of the next
for execution means the word is beheaded, losing its first letter

parts.note: heaves means throws
the drop is the trapdoor through which a hanged person falls

explanation.surface: A secret hearing ends in a hanging, with the condemned dropped through the trapdoor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For execution' means HEAVES is beheaded, giving EAVES. The definition means listening in secret, not a closed court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation.

clue.text: What Lowry created on the slopes, of Etna?

definitions.text: What Lowry created on the slopes, of Etna?

parts.words: What Lowry created on the slopes, of Etna?
parts.note: suggests the painter L. S. Lowry at work on a mountainside, but points to Malcolm Lowry's novel title, which describes the position of anyone on Etna's slopes

explanation.surface: The painter Lowry sets up his easel on the slopes of Etna.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowry suggests L. S. Lowry, the English painter of industrial scenes; the novelist Malcolm Lowry wrote the 1947 novel set in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm Lowry's best-known novel bears this title, which also describes being on a volcano's slopes.

clue.text: High-class criminal's charity events

definitions.meaning: the gentleman thief created by E. W. Hornung, a cricketing burglar; the possessive s is part of the name
draws in which tickets are sold to win prizes, often to raise money for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Raffles is both Hornung's gentleman burglar and the word for prize draws held for charity.

clue.text: Shifty copper caught up in nasty hole

indicators.note: in means the turned symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
nasty means the letters of hole are made into a mess and rearranged
in a down clue, caught up means the copper symbol is turned to read upwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A dodgy policeman is trapped in a horrible pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the letters into LOHE and 'caught up' turns the symbol to UC. 'Copper' suggests a policeman but means the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or of dubious character, close to shifty.

clue.text: From box, one heard interrupting concert?

indicators.note: heard means the clue's description is said out loud and gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: one interrupting a concert might be someone with a cough, a cougher

explanation.surface: A box at the theatre, from which one audience member is heard disrupting the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' belongs with 'interrupting concert': a person who coughs through a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for holding money and valuables.

clue.text: Passenger redirected a short way in the up direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, the up direction means the run of letters is read upwards
a short way in means the letters are found just inside the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A traveller is sent a short way in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: REDIR sits at the start of 'redirected'; read upwards it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is someone carried in or on a vehicle, a passenger.

clue.text: Most unpleasant holiday on very little money

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a sou was a French coin of very small value, so not a sou means almost no money
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: A holiday taken on next to no money is the grimmest kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourest is the superlative of sour, meaning most disagreeable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Dirty hole, but we live here

definitions.meaning: a fox's den in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a burrow dug by a fox and the planet we live on.

clue.text: Counter a lofted 29

definitions.meaning: a gambling token used in place of money
29 across is a shot; a lofted shot in golf or football is one lifted high

explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a casino token and also a short lofted stroke in golf.

clue.text: In dining room, a specially-prepared meat

indicators.note: In means the letter a is put inside the word for dining room

parts.note: a hall is a large dining room, as in a college hall

explanation.surface: In the dining hall, a specially prepared meat dish is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat comes from animals slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic law.

clue.text: Brown heroin? Little is known of its properties

definitions.text: Little is known of its properties

parts.note: dark can describe a brown colour or complexion
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Brown heroin is a mystery substance whose effects are little understood.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a note on a drug, but describes a racehorse, or a contender, whose ability is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor whose form and abilities are unknown to most is called this, from horse racing.

clue.text: Send off exam answers for belated comment

parts.note: to post is to send off by mail
a script is a candidate's written answers in an exam

explanation.surface: Posting off exam papers prompts a last-minute remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is an afterthought added at the end of a letter, a comment made late.

clue.text: Photograph rocket launch

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a snapshot and a launch such as a moon shot.
